units.leftText: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ according to the commandment of God our Savior and the Lord Jesus Christ our hope,
units.rightText: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus according to the commandment of God our Saviour, and Christ Jesus our hope;
leftNotes: 1:1 NU reads Christ Jesus and omits the Lord.

units.leftText: to Timothy, my true child in faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
units.rightText: unto Timothy, my true child in faith: Grace, mercy, peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.leftText: As I urged you when I was going into Macedonia, stay at Ephesus that you might command certain men not to teach a different doctrine,
units.rightText: As I exhorted thee to tarry at Ephesus, when I was going into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge certain men not to teach a different doctrine,

units.leftText: and not to pay attention to myths and endless genealogies, which cause disputes rather than God’s stewardship, which is in faith.
units.rightText: neither to give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questionings, rather than a dispensation of God which is in faith; so do I now.

units.leftText: But the goal of this command is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith,
units.rightText: But the end of the charge is love out of a pure heart and a good conscience and faith unfeigned:

units.leftText: from which things some, having missed the mark, have turned away to vain talking,
units.rightText: from which things some having swerved have turned aside unto vain talking;

units.leftText: desiring to be teachers of the law, though they understand neither what they say nor about what they strongly affirm.
units.rightText: desiring to be teachers of the law, though they understand neither what they say, nor whereof they confidently affirm.

units.leftText: But we know that the law is good if a person uses it lawfully,
units.rightText: But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully,

units.leftText: as knowing this, that law is not made for a righteous person, but for the lawless and insubordinate, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,
units.rightText: as knowing this, that law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and unruly, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,

units.leftText: for the sexually immoral, for homosexuals, for slave-traders, for liars, for perjurers, and for any other thing contrary to the sound doctrine,
units.rightText: for fornicators, for abusers of themselves with men, for menstealers, for liars, for false swearers, and if there be any other thing contrary to the sound doctrine;

units.leftText: according to the Good News of the glory of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.
units.rightText: according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.

units.leftText: I thank him who enabled me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he counted me faithful, appointing me to service,
units.rightText: I thank him that enabled me, even Christ Jesus our Lord, for that he counted me faithful, appointing me to his service;

units.leftText: although I used to be a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent. However, I obtained mercy because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
units.rightText: though I was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: howbeit I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief;

units.leftText: The grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: and the grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: The saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief.
units.rightText: Faithful is the saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief:

units.leftText: However, for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first, Jesus Christ might display all his patience for an example of those who were going to believe in him for eternal life.
units.rightText: howbeit for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me as chief might Jesus Christ show forth all his longsuffering, for an ensample of them that should thereafter believe on him unto eternal life.

units.leftText: Now to the King eternal, immortal, invisible, to God who alone is wise, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
units.rightText: Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

units.leftText: I commit this instruction to you, my child Timothy, according to the prophecies which were given to you before, that by them you may wage the good warfare,
units.rightText: This charge I commit unto thee, my child Timothy, according to the prophecies which led the way to thee, that by them thou mayest war the good warfare;

units.leftText: holding faith and a good conscience, which some having thrust away made a shipwreck concerning the faith,
units.rightText: holding faith and a good conscience; which some having thrust from them made shipwreck concerning the faith:

units.leftText: of whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I delivered to Satan that they might be taught not to blaspheme.
units.rightText: of whom is Hymenæus and Alexander; whom I delivered unto Satan, that they might be taught not to blaspheme.

units.leftText: I exhort therefore, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks be made for all men,
units.rightText: I exhort therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, thanksgivings, be made for all men;

units.leftText: for kings and all who are in high places, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and reverence.
units.rightText: for kings and all that are in high place; that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and gravity.

units.leftText: For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior,
units.rightText: This is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour;

units.leftText: who desires all people to be saved and come to full knowledge of the truth.
units.rightText: who would have all men to be saved, and come to the knowledge of the truth.

units.leftText: For there is one God and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus,
units.rightText: For there is one God, one mediator also between God and men, himself man, Christ Jesus,

units.leftText: who gave himself as a ransom for all, the testimony at the proper time,
units.rightText: who gave himself a ransom for all; the testimony to be borne in its own times;

units.leftText: to which I was appointed a preacher and an apostle—I am telling the truth in Christ, not lying—a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
units.rightText: whereunto I was appointed a preacher and an apostle (I speak the truth, I lie not), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.

units.leftText: I desire therefore that the men in every place pray, lifting up holy hands without anger and doubting.
units.rightText: I desire therefore that the men pray in every place, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and disputing.

units.leftText: In the same way, that women also adorn themselves in decent clothing, with modesty and propriety, not with braided hair, gold, pearls, or expensive clothing,
units.rightText: In like manner, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefastness and sobriety; not with braided hair, and gold or pearls or costly raiment;
leftNotes: 2:9 The word for “not” is the negative particle “μη” which denies an expected idea, as opposed to the usual word for “not” (ου) which denies a fact. Thus “μη” in this context is denying an expected idea (that women can be properly dressed without good works).

units.leftText: but with good works, which is appropriate for women professing godliness.
units.rightText: but (which becometh women professing godliness) through good works.

units.leftText: Let a woman learn in quietness with full submission.
units.rightText: Let a woman learn in quietness with all subjection.

units.leftText: But I don’t permit a woman to teach, nor to exercise authority over a man, but to be in quietness.
units.rightText: But I permit not a woman to teach, nor to have dominion over a man, but to be in quietness.

units.leftText: For Adam was formed first, then Eve.
units.rightText: For Adam was first formed, then Eve;

units.leftText: Adam wasn’t deceived, but the woman, being deceived, has fallen into disobedience;
units.rightText: and Adam was not beguiled, but the woman being beguiled hath fallen into transgression:

units.leftText: but she will be saved through her childbearing, if they continue in faith, love, and holiness with sobriety.
units.rightText: but she shall be saved through her child-bearing, if they continue in faith and love and sanctification with sobriety.

units.leftText: This is a faithful saying: someone who seeks to be an overseer desires a good work.
units.rightText: Faithful is the saying, If a man seeketh the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.

units.leftText: The overseer therefore must be without reproach, the husband of one wife, temperate, sensible, modest, hospitable, good at teaching;
units.rightText: The bishop therefore must be without reproach, the husband of one wife, temperate, sober-minded, orderly, given to hospitality, apt to teach;

units.leftText: not a drinker, not violent, not greedy for money, but gentle, not quarrelsome, not covetous;
units.rightText: no brawler, no striker; but gentle, not contentious, no lover of money;

units.leftText: one who rules his own house well, having children in subjection with all reverence;
units.rightText: one that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity;

units.leftText: (for how could someone who doesn’t know how to rule his own house take care of God’s assembly?)
units.rightText: (but if a man knoweth not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?)

units.leftText: not a new convert, lest being puffed up he fall into the same condemnation as the devil.
units.rightText: not a novice, lest being puffed up he fall into the condemnation of the devil.

units.leftText: Moreover he must have good testimony from those who are outside, to avoid falling into reproach and the snare of the devil.
units.rightText: Moreover he must have good testimony from them that are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.

units.leftText: Servants, in the same way, must be reverent, not double-tongued, not addicted to much wine, not greedy for money,
units.rightText: Deacons in like manner must be grave, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre;

units.leftText: holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
units.rightText: holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.

units.leftText: Let them also first be tested; then let them serve if they are blameless.
units.rightText: And let these also first be proved; then let them serve as deacons, if they be blameless.

units.leftText: Their wives in the same way must be reverent, not slanderers, temperate, and faithful in all things.
units.rightText: Women in like manner must be grave, not slanderers, temperate, faithful in all things.

units.leftText: Let servants be husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.
units.rightText: Let deacons be husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.

units.leftText: For those who have served well gain for themselves a good standing and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: For they that have served well as deacons gain to themselves a good standing, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: These things I write to you, hoping to come to you shortly,
units.rightText: These things write I unto thee, hoping to come unto thee shortly;

units.leftText: but if I wait long, that you may know how men ought to behave themselves in God’s house, which is the assembly of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.
units.rightText: but if I tarry long, that thou mayest know how men ought to behave themselves in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.

units.leftText: Without controversy, the mystery of godliness is great:
units.rightText: And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness;

units.leftText: But the Spirit says expressly that in later times some will fall away from the faith, paying attention to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons,
units.rightText: But the Spirit saith expressly, that in later times some shall fall away from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons,

units.leftText: through the hypocrisy of men who speak lies, branded in their own conscience as with a hot iron,
units.rightText: through the hypocrisy of men that speak lies, branded in their own conscience as with a hot iron;

units.leftText: forbidding marriage and commanding to abstain from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
units.rightText: forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God created to be received with thanksgiving by them that believe and know the truth.

units.leftText: For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving.
units.rightText: For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected, if it be received with thanksgiving:

units.leftText: For it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.
units.rightText: for it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.

units.leftText: If you instruct the brothers of these things, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished in the words of the faith and of the good doctrine which you have followed.
units.rightText: If thou put the brethren in mind of these things, thou shalt be a good minister of Christ Jesus, nourished in the words of the faith, and of the good doctrine which thou hast followed until now:

units.leftText: But refuse profane and old wives’ fables. Exercise yourself toward godliness.
units.rightText: but refuse profane and old wives’ fables. And exercise thyself unto godliness:

units.leftText: For bodily exercise has some value, but godliness has value in all things, having the promise of the life which is now and of that which is to come.
units.rightText: for bodily exercise is profitable for a little; but godliness is profitable for all things, having promise of the life which now is, and of that which is to come.

units.leftText: This saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance.
units.rightText: Faithful is the saying, and worthy of all acceptation.

units.leftText: For to this end we both labor and suffer reproach, because we have set our trust in the living God, who is the Savior of all men, especially of those who believe.
units.rightText: For to this end we labor and strive, because we have our hope set on the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of them that believe.

units.leftText: Command and teach these things.
units.rightText: These things command and teach.

units.leftText: Let no man despise your youth; but be an example to those who believe, in word, in your way of life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.
units.rightText: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an ensample to them that believe, in word, in manner of life, in love, in faith, in purity.

units.leftText: Until I come, pay attention to reading, to exhortation, and to teaching.
units.rightText: Till I come, give heed to reading, to exhortation, to teaching.

units.leftText: Don’t neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you by prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the elders.
units.rightText: Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.

units.leftText: Be diligent in these things. Give yourself wholly to them, that your progress may be revealed to all.
units.rightText: Be diligent in these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy progress may be manifest unto all.

units.leftText: Pay attention to yourself and to your teaching. Continue in these things, for in doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you.
units.rightText: Take heed to thyself, and to thy teaching. Continue in these things; for in doing this thou shalt save both thyself and them that hear thee.

units.leftText: Don’t rebuke an older man, but exhort him as a father; the younger men as brothers;
units.rightText: Rebuke not an elder, but exhort him as a father; the younger men as brethren:

units.leftText: the elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, in all purity.
units.rightText: the elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, in all purity.

units.leftText: Honor widows who are widows indeed.
units.rightText: Honor widows that are widows indeed.

units.leftText: But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them learn first to show piety toward their own family and to repay their parents, for this is acceptable in the sight of God.
units.rightText: But if any widow hath children or grandchildren, let them learn first to show piety towards their own family, and to requite their parents: for this is acceptable in the sight of God.

units.leftText: Now she who is a widow indeed and desolate, has her hope set on God and continues in petitions and prayers night and day.
units.rightText: Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, hath her hope set on God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.

units.leftText: But she who gives herself to pleasure is dead while she lives.
units.rightText: But she that giveth herself to pleasure is dead while she liveth.

units.leftText: Also command these things, that they may be without reproach.
units.rightText: These things also command, that they may be without reproach.

units.leftText: But if anyone doesn’t provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
units.rightText: But if any provideth not for his own, and specially his own household, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an unbeliever.

units.leftText: Let no one be enrolled as a widow under sixty years old, having been the wife of one man,
units.rightText: Let none be enrolled as a widow under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man,

units.leftText: being approved by good works, if she has brought up children, if she has been hospitable to strangers, if she has washed the saints’ feet, if she has relieved the afflicted, and if she has diligently followed every good work.
units.rightText: well reported of for good works; if she hath brought up children, if she hath used hospitality to strangers, if she hath washed the saints’ feet, if she hath relieved the afflicted, if she hath diligently followed every good work.

units.leftText: But refuse younger widows, for when they have grown wanton against Christ, they desire to marry,
units.rightText: But younger widows refuse: for when they have waxed wanton against Christ, they desire to marry;

units.leftText: having condemnation, because they have rejected their first pledge.
units.rightText: having condemnation, because they have rejected their first pledge.

units.leftText: Besides, they also learn to be idle, going about from house to house. Not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, saying things which they ought not.
units.rightText: And withal they learn also to be idle, going about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.

units.leftText: I desire therefore that the younger widows marry, bear children, rule the household, and give no occasion to the adversary for insulting.
units.rightText: I desire therefore that the younger widows marry, bear children, rule the household, give no occasion to the adversary for reviling:

units.leftText: For already some have turned away after Satan.
units.rightText: for already some are turned aside after Satan.

units.leftText: If any man or woman who believes has widows, let them relieve them, and don’t let the assembly be burdened, that it might relieve those who are widows indeed.
units.rightText: If any woman that believeth hath widows, let her relieve them, and let not the church be burdened; that it may relieve them that are widows indeed.

units.leftText: Let the elders who rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in the word and in teaching.
units.rightText: Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in the word and in teaching.

units.leftText: For the Scripture says, “You shall not muzzle the ox when it treads out the grain.” And, “The laborer is worthy of his wages.”
units.rightText: For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn. And, The laborer is worthy of his hire.

units.leftText: Don’t receive an accusation against an elder except at the word of two or three witnesses.
units.rightText: Against an elder receive not an accusation, except at the mouth of two or three witnesses.

units.leftText: Those who sin, reprove in the sight of all, that the rest also may be in fear.
units.rightText: Them that sin reprove in the sight of all, that the rest also may be in fear.

units.leftText: I command you in the sight of God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the chosen angels, that you observe these things without prejudice, doing nothing by partiality.
units.rightText: I charge thee in the sight of God, and Christ Jesus, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without prejudice, doing nothing by partiality.

units.leftText: Lay hands hastily on no one. Don’t be a participant in other people’s sins. Keep yourself pure.
units.rightText: Lay hands hastily on no man, neither be partaker of other men’s sins: keep thyself pure.

units.leftText: Be no longer a drinker of water only, but use a little wine for your stomach’s sake and your frequent infirmities.
units.rightText: Be no longer a drinker of water, but use a little wine for thy stomach’s sake and thine often infirmities.

units.leftText: Some men’s sins are evident, preceding them to judgment, and some also follow later.
units.rightText: Some men’s sins are evident, going before unto judgment; and some men also they follow after.

units.leftText: In the same way also there are good works that are obvious, and those that are otherwise can’t be hidden.
units.rightText: In like manner also there are good works that are evident; and such as are otherwise cannot be hid.

units.leftText: Let as many as are bondservants under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honor, that the name of God and the doctrine not be blasphemed.
units.rightText: Let as many as are servants under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honor, that the name of God and the doctrine be not blasphemed.

units.leftText: Those who have believing masters, let them not despise them because they are brothers, but rather let them serve them, because those who partake of the benefit are believing and beloved. Teach and exhort these things.
units.rightText: And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren; but let them serve them the rather, because they that partake of the benefit are believing and beloved. These things teach and exhort.

units.leftText: If anyone teaches a different doctrine and doesn’t consent to sound words, the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness,
units.rightText: If any man teacheth a different doctrine, and consenteth not to sound words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness;

units.leftText: he is conceited, knowing nothing, but obsessed with arguments, disputes, and word battles, from which come envy, strife, insulting, evil suspicions,
units.rightText: he is puffed up, knowing nothing, but doting about questionings and disputes of words, whereof cometh envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings,

units.leftText: constant friction of people of corrupt minds and destitute of the truth, who suppose that godliness is a means of gain. Withdraw yourself from such.
units.rightText: wranglings of men corrupted in mind and bereft of the truth, supposing that godliness is a way of gain.

units.leftText: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
units.rightText: But godliness with contentment is great gain:

units.leftText: For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can’t carry anything out.
units.rightText: for we brought nothing into the world, for neither can we carry anything out;

units.leftText: But having food and clothing, we will be content with that.
units.rightText: but having food and covering we shall be therewith content.

units.leftText: But those who are determined to be rich fall into a temptation, a snare, and many foolish and harmful lusts, such as drown men in ruin and destruction.
units.rightText: But they that are minded to be rich fall into a temptation and a snare and many foolish and hurtful lusts, such as drown men in destruction and perdition.

units.leftText: For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some have been led astray from the faith in their greed, and have pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
units.rightText: For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil: which some reaching after have been led astray from the faith, and have pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

units.leftText: But you, man of God, flee these things, and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.
units.rightText: But thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness.

units.leftText: Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called, and you confessed the good confession in the sight of many witnesses.
units.rightText: Fight the good fight of the faith, lay hold on the life eternal, whereunto thou wast called, and didst confess the good confession in the sight of many witnesses.

units.leftText: I command you before God who gives life to all things, and before Christ Jesus who before Pontius Pilate testified the good confession,
units.rightText: I charge thee in the sight of God, who giveth life to all things, and of Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed the good confession;

units.leftText: that you keep the commandment without spot, blameless until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
units.rightText: that thou keep the commandment, without spot, without reproach, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ:

units.leftText: which at the right time he will show, who is the blessed and only Ruler, the King of kings and Lord of lords.
units.rightText: which in its own times he shall show, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;

units.leftText: He alone has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no man has seen nor can see, to whom be honor and eternal power. Amen.
units.rightText: who only hath immortality, dwelling in light unapproachable; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honor and power eternal. Amen.

units.leftText: Charge those who are rich in this present age that they not be arrogant, nor have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on the living God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy;
units.rightText: Charge them that are rich in this present world, that they be not highminded, nor have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy;

units.leftText: that they do good, that they be rich in good works, that they be ready to distribute, willing to share;
units.rightText: that they do good, that they be rich in good works, that they be ready to distribute, willing to communicate;

units.leftText: laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold of eternal life.
units.rightText: laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on the life which is life indeed.

units.leftText: Timothy, guard that which is committed to you, turning away from the empty chatter and oppositions of what is falsely called knowledge,
units.rightText: O Timothy, guard that which is committed unto thee, turning away from the profane babblings and oppositions of the knowledge which is falsely so called;

units.leftText: which some profess, and thus have wandered from the faith.
units.rightText: which some professing have erred concerning the faith.
